title: "All Objects" Table-Scan Query
pattern: Querying the database to instantiate all records of a table/entity into memory as objects, and then selecting or aggregating only a fraction of their fields.
why_bad: High memory exhaustion risk. It bypasses database-level indexing and aggregation capabilities, fetching massive datasets across the network and instantiating thousands of objects, easily causing Out-Of-Memory (OOM) crashes in production.
detection: Calling a repository finder method named `find_all()` or returning an unbounded list, followed by an immediate filter, map, or fold operation on the in-memory collection.
counterexample: A lookup on a small, statically-bounded lookup table (e.g., list of active US states).
fix: Express the filter or aggregation directly as a database-level query (e.g., using `SUM` or `WHERE` clauses).
